chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Husayn ibn Usman from Ibn Muskan from Aban ibn Taghlib said,

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him) placed a brick upon the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So I said, 'What is your view if a man were to place a brick upon him, would it harm the deceased?' He said: 'No'.

key_terms.آجُرٌّ: A brick, plural of جُرْجُرَة or variant of لَبِن, referring to a building block.
key_terms.النَّبِيُّ: The Prophet, specifically referring to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) in this context.
key_terms.لَبِنٌ: A brick or slab of baked clay used for construction or marking.

ai.seo_question: Does placing a brick or slab on a grave harm the deceased according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the permissibility of elevating graves with markers like bricks or slabs, using the precedent of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) placing a slab on the Prophet’s grave. It clarifies that such structural additions do not harm the deceased, thereby validating the architectural practice of raising graves for identification and reverence in Shia tradition.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Husayn Bin Usman, from Ibn Muskan, from Aban Bin Taghlib who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> made a slab to be upon the grave of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>’. So I said, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view if the man were to make a brick to be upon him, would it harm the deceased?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
